chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) mentioning that an Angel came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives you a choice: that you be a servant, a humble messenger, or a king, a messenger.' He said: So he looked at Jibreel and gestured with his hand [signaling] to be humble, so he said: 'A servant, a humble messenger.' The Messenger said, 'Along with that, nothing will be diminished from what is with your Lord.' He said: 'And with him were the keys of the treasures of the earth.'
ai.seo_question: What choice was given to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) regarding his prophetic role?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is presented with a divine choice between being a 'servant-messenger' characterized by humility or a 'king-messenger' endowed with worldly power. He selects the former, affirming that true prophetic status lies in servitude rather than sovereignty, a choice validated by the angel who notes that this humility does not diminish his standing with God despite the presence of the 'keys to the earth's treasures.' This event underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s voluntary adoption of humility as the pinnacle of spiritual authority, distinguishing it from the kingly arrogance often associated with pre-Islamic or contemporary rulers.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> mentioning that an Angel came over to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and he said, ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Gives you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> choice – you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> can either become a servant, a humble Rasool<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>’ or to be an angel and a messenger. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> looked at Jibraeel<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and gestured with his<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> hand in humbleness, so he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘A servant, a humble Rasool<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>’. So he (the Angel) said, ‘The Rasool<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, along with that there would be no reduction from what is there for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> in the Presence of your<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> by antyhing’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And with him (the Angel) were the keys of the treasures of the earth’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ibn Faddal from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘Once an angel came to the Messenger of Allah and said, ‘‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, gives you the choice to be a servant and a humble messenger, or to be an angel and a messenger.” He looked to Jibril who made a gesture with his hand to be humble. He (the Messenger of Allah) said, “I want to be a humble servant and a messenger.” The messenger (the angel) said, “Despite this, there is no reduction in what is with your Lord.” The Imam said, “With him were the keys to the treasures of earth.’””
